clue.text: Dreadful combat with man leading mass slaughter

indicators.note: leading means the man's pronoun goes at the front of the rearranged letters

parts.note: HE is the pronoun for a man

indicators.note: dreadful suggests something mangled out of shape, so the letters of combat are rearranged

explanation.surface: A grim battle, with soldiers at the front, ends in a massacre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dreadful' looks like it describes the battle but signals the anagram (CATOMB); 'leading' fronts it with the man.
explanation.definitionFit: A hecatomb was originally a sacrifice of a hundred oxen, and by extension any great slaughter.

clue.text: Pound for a good book?

definitions.meaning: the first name of the American poet Pound
a book of the Bible, the Good Book

explanation.definitionFit: Ezra was the poet Pound's first name and is the title of an Old Testament book.

clue.text: Creature's lair disturbed inside it's angry, see

definitions.note: the possessive of creature stands for the answer followed by is

indicators.note: inside it's means the next word goes within the rearranged letters
disturbed means the letters of lair are knocked out of order

parts.note: mad means angry
lo is an old word for look or see

explanation.surface: An animal's den is upset and, inside, its owner is furious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Creature's' is the definition plus 'is'; 'disturbed' gives ARIL and 'inside it's' places the anger within it, with 'see' tacked on.
explanation.definitionFit: An armadillo is an armoured burrowing mammal of the Americas, a creature.

clue.text: Admitting missing entrance to Cambridge college

indicators.note: missing the entrance means losing the first letter of the college name

parts.note: Downing is one of the colleges of Cambridge University

explanation.surface: An applicant confesses to failing to get into a Cambridge college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing entrance to' removes the first letter of DOWNING, a Cambridge college; 'entrance' looks like university admission.
explanation.definitionFit: Owning up means admitting, and owning alone carries that sense of acknowledging something.

clue.text: Flowers put into ground shortly sprout up in artistic circle

parts.note: blooms are flowers
to bury is to put something into the ground

indicators.note: shortly asks for the word to be cut short by its last letter

parts.note: to grow is to sprout
taken as written

explanation.surface: A gardener plants flowers which soon shoot up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' cuts GROW to GRO. The Bloomsbury Group was an early twentieth-century London set of writers and artists including Virginia Woolf.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bloomsbury Group was a famous circle of English writers, painters and thinkers, an artistic coterie.

clue.text: Good bowling before batsman finally is in control

indicators.note: before places the bowling ahead of the batsman's letter in the answer

parts.note: in cricket an over is a spell of six balls bowled by one bowler

indicators.note: finally picks out the very last letter of the word batsman

explanation.surface: A cricket report: tight bowling and a batsman out at last leave one side in command.
explanation.walkthrough: An OVER is a set of six deliveries in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: To govern is to rule or be in control of something, so the verb phrase is a synonym.

clue.text: South American man has seen a revolution

parts.note: a guy is a man

indicators.note: a revolution turns things upside down, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man from South America has witnessed an uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolution' turns SEEN A into ANESE; 'has' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A Guyanese person comes from Guyana, a country on the north coast of South America.

clue.text: Raven, essentially close relative to crow

indicators.note: essentially points to the essence or core of the word, its middle letter

parts.note: an aunt is a close family member

explanation.surface: A bird-watcher notes the raven is basically a near relation of the crow.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface sets up birds, but 'crow' is the verb meaning to boast.
explanation.definitionFit: To crow is to boast triumphantly, and to vaunt is likewise to brag.

clue.text: Brute is soon richer, after dubious dealing

indicators.note: dubious dealing suggests the letters are shuffled like a crooked hand of cards

explanation.surface: A villain expects to be rich soon after some shady business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' links definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A brute is a large wild beast, and the rhinoceros is a classic example of one.

clue.text: Briefly walk all over right-wing head

indicators.note: briefly asks for a word cut short, so the seaside walk loses its ending

parts.note: a promenade is a walk, especially along a seafront
to be on something is to be all over it, covering it
a Tory is a member of Britain's right-wing Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A political sketch: a conservative leader tramples over everyone in his path.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Briefly' shortens PROMENADE to PROM, the British word for a seafront walk; 'head' is not a leader but a headland.
explanation.definitionFit: A head in geography is a headland, a high point of land jutting into the sea, which is exactly a promontory.

clue.text: Uranium metal brought over in quantity

parts.note: U is the chemical symbol for uranium

indicators.note: brought over means the metal's name is turned round and read backwards

parts.note: tin is a metal

explanation.surface: A chemistry note about uranium and another metal being shipped in bulk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought over' turns TIN into NIT.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit is a fixed quantity used as a standard of measurement.

clue.text: Command to arrest extremists of eastern sect

indicators.note: to arrest is to seize and hold, so the outer word takes the letters into custody inside it

parts.note: domination is command or control over others

indicators.note: the extremists of a word are its first and last letters, here E and N

explanation.surface: An order goes out to round up the radicals of an Eastern religious group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to arrest' suggests police, but just means the command word holds the outer letters of 'eastern' after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A denomination is a distinct religious body within a faith, much like a sect.

clue.text: Spray, as Ancient Mariner did wedding guests?

definitions.meaning: a small bunch of flowers worn on a lapel

definitions.text: as Ancient Mariner did wedding guests?
definitions.meaning: in Coleridge's poem the mariner stops a guest and detains him to tell his story

explanation.definitionFit: A buttonhole is a lapel flower spray, and to buttonhole is to waylay someone in talk as Coleridge's mariner does.

clue.text: Consider island warm?

definitions.meaning: an island of the Inner Hebrides off western Scotland
to heat wine or ale with spices, as for a winter drink

explanation.definitionFit: Mull means to ponder, is a Scottish island, and to heat spiced wine, three separate senses of one word.

clue.text: Mad to be outwitted about a piece of scripture

indicators.note: about means the outwitted word goes round the scripture letters

parts.note: to be bested is to be outdone or outwitted
OT, the Old Testament, is a part of the Bible

explanation.surface: Someone is driven mad at being outsmarted in an argument over a Bible passage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps the outwitted word round the Old Testament; 'to be' is a link, and 'Mad' means infatuated.
explanation.definitionFit: Besotted means infatuated to the point of foolishness, a crossword-friendly sense of mad, as in mad about someone.

clue.text: One makes sporting admission in revolutionary manner

definitions.text: One makes sporting admission in revolutionary manner

parts.words: One makes sporting admission in revolutionary manner
parts.note: a rotating gate that lets spectators into a sports ground one at a time, turning as each passes

explanation.definitionFit: A turnstile is a revolving gate that admits people one by one, as at football grounds.

clue.text: Maker of sharp climb may go into tailspin

indicators.note: may go into suggests the letters spiral wildly out of order like a plane in trouble

explanation.surface: A mountaineer on a steep ascent risks spinning out of control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may go into' signals that TAILSPIN is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: An alpinist is a mountain climber, someone who makes steep ascents.

clue.text: One taking constitutional way to overturn monarch

parts.note: St, short for street, is a way
to roll over is to overturn, and roll alone carries that sense
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword monarch

explanation.surface: A political tale of plotting a route to topple the Crown.
explanation.walkthrough: A constitutional is a walk taken for one's health, so 'constitutional' is not about politics; ER stands for the Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: A stroller is someone walking at leisure, just as a person taking a constitutional takes a gentle healthy walk.

clue.text: Firmly establish sound course

indicators.note: sound means the word for a course is said out loud and spelt differently

parts.note: a route is a course to follow

explanation.surface: A plain instruction to set up a reliable path.
explanation.walkthrough: ROUTE is said like ROOT in British speech.
explanation.definitionFit: To root an idea or plant is to fix it firmly in place, establishing it.

clue.text: One shaping to provide fine seafood

parts.note: F is the pencil-grading abbreviation for fine
an ormer is an edible shellfish, the abalone of the Channel Islands

explanation.surface: A craftsman makes a living supplying good shellfish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to provide' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A former is a tool or person that gives shape to something.

clue.text: Musical without standards? Yes and no

definitions.meaning: a Cole Porter stage show of 1934
a phrase meaning no rules apply, so both yes and no are acceptable

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names a famous Cole Porter musical and also means that every behaviour is allowed.

clue.text: Following breach of duty, European becomes tart

indicators.note: following means the European letter is placed after the legal wrong

parts.note: in law a tort is a civil wrong, a breach of a duty owed

explanation.surface: A European turns sour after neglecting his obligations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tart' looks like an adjective meaning sour but is a pastry.
explanation.definitionFit: A torte is a rich cake or tart, often with a pastry base.

clue.text: It's fresh each time

parts.note: per means for each, as in per person

explanation.surface: Something stays new every single time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fresh' means cheeky, not new; 'It's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Fresh can mean cheeky or impudent, and pert describes a saucily bold manner.

clue.text: The head for drink Falstaff had — nothing remains in pub

definitions.text: The head for drink Falstaff had

indicators.note: remains in means the zero letter sits inside the pub word

parts.note: a bar is a pub
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A tale of Falstaff's favourite tavern, where nothing is left to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: In Shakespeare's Henry IV Falstaff drinks at the Boar's Head tavern, so the definition reads 'the [___]'s Head'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Boar's Head was the Eastcheap tavern where Shakespeare sets Falstaff's drinking, so the animal fills that tavern name.

clue.text: Girl goes to press in case of torture

indicators.note: goes to means the girl is attached after the pressing word

parts.note: to iron clothes is to press them
a maiden is a girl

explanation.surface: A young woman takes her story to the newspapers about a torture case.
explanation.walkthrough: An iron maiden was a hinged case lined with spikes, used as an instrument of torture.
explanation.definitionFit: The iron maiden was a spiked cabinet in which victims were enclosed, a literal case for torture.

clue.text: Failing to change allegiance

definitions.meaning: to desert one's country or side for another

explanation.definitionFit: Defect is a noun for a fault and a verb meaning to switch sides, two unrelated senses.

clue.text: Smoke ring by absolute beginner

indicators.note: beginner marks the absolute word as coming first, before the ring

parts.note: perfect can mean absolute, as in a perfect stranger
O is shaped like a ring

explanation.surface: A novice tries to blow a smoke ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by absolute beginner' says the ring comes with PERFECT at the start.
explanation.definitionFit: A perfecto is a type of cigar thick in the middle and tapered at both ends, something one smokes.
